Drop factor levels without observations before fitting a Cox model

Source: R/fit_utils.R
drop_empty_levels.Rd

survival::coxph(), survival::clogit() and coxme::coxme() keep the levels of a factor that have no observations among the complete cases of the model, where lm(), glm() and lme4 drop them from the model frame. An empty level is then aliased; when it is the first level, the other levels are estimated against whichever of them is aliased in turn (see effective_reference_level()), and coxme() fails to fit. The empty levels of the factors that a model uses are therefore dropped before a Cox model is fitted, so that it takes the first level with observations as its reference, as the other models do.

Usage

drop_empty_levels(data, terms)

Arguments

data

Data table.

terms

Character vector of the terms of the model, such as the outcome, predictors, random effects, strata and cluster variable, from which the variables are read.

Value

data when none of its factors among the variables has an empty level, and otherwise a copy in which they have none.

Details

A level counts as empty when no complete case of the model variables takes it, as for the model frame of glm(), so that a level that occurs only in observations excluded for missing values is dropped as well. Those observations, which the model does not use, are then missing for the factor; the attributes of the factor, such as a variable label, are kept.
